images.caption: Pockmarked sands, Nanjizal beach The sand here is exposed by the ebbing tide and it has been pockmarked by the feet of the various visitors since the last high tide. The low angle of the sun emphasises the hundreds of tiny depressions. The sloping cliff beyond is Higher Bosistow Cliff, and the slot-like natural arch is known as Zawn Pyg.

images.filename: Sandy beach in Nanjizal Bay (or Mill Bay) - geograph.org.uk - 526237.jpg
images.caption:
Sandy beach in Nanjizal Bay (or Mill Bay) This beach is only a mile or so south of the Lands End tourist trap, but as it is not served by any roads or car parks, and can only really be reached by a hilly walk along the coastal footpath, it is not busy with tourists - even in high season. The amount of sand on the beach varies - apparently much of it was stripped away in a storm a few years ago, but it is being replenished by natural processes.
The sands here feature in one variation on the folklore tale of Jan Tregeagle. It is said that his Sisyphean task is to try and sweep the sand from Porthcurno cove around the Gwennap Head into Nanjizal Bay. On stormy winter nights you can hear him howling with despair at the futility of his task.

The bay is also known as "Mill Bay", after the mill just above the beach that was driven by water from the stream which cascades down the cliff. The fresh water disappears below the sand and at low tide emerges further down the beach when it meets the underlying rock.

images.filename: Sea-worn granite boulders exposed by low tide, Nanjizal bay - geograph.org.uk - 526245.jpg
images.caption: Sea-worn granite boulders exposed by low tide, Nanjizal bay These boulders at the foot of the cliffs have been rounded and smoothed by the action of the sea over hundreds of years. Here they are exposed by the low tide, and their surfaces are slippery with seaweed. On the other side of the beach is Higher Bosistow Cliff and the chasm of Zawn Pyg.coa

images.filename: View of Mill Bay from a cave, Nanjizal - geograph.org.uk - 526248.jpg
images.caption: View of Mill Bay from a cave, Nanjizal Later on when the tide comes back in the sea will re-enter this cave in Lower Bosistow Cliff, which opens out on to the sandy tidal beach at Nanjizal. The sandy floor in the cave is marked with the footprints of all who have visited since the last high tide.
